header.running_head: Rasulullaah ﷺ is Particular about Dispatching the Army of Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) even on his Deathbed, after which Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) also Gives the Same Importance to the Matter When he Becomes the Khalifah

Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then left the house and instructed someone to announce, "I strongly emphasise that no one who had marched with Usaama during the lifetime of Rasulullaah ﷺ should remain behind. If anyone is brought to me who had stayed behind, I shall make him join the army on foot." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then sent for those Muhaajireen who objected to the appointment of Hadhrat Usaama (RA) as Ameer. He was stern with them and took an undertaking from them that they will march with Hadhrat Usaama (RA). Consequently, not a soul stayed behind.
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then left to see Hadhrat Usaama (RA) and the Muslims off. When they left from Jurf, they numbered three thousand men and had a thousand horses. As they rode off, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) walked by the side of Hadhrat Usaama (RA) for a while and said to him, "I entrust to Allaah your Deen, your belongings and the result of your actions. Rasulullaah ﷺ has already briefed you, so fulfil the instructions of Rasulullaah ﷺ. I shall neither command nor prevent you from proceeding for I am merely executing the instruction that Rasulullaah ﷺ issued."
Hadhrat Usaama (RA) set off speedily and passed through peaceful areas where the people had not forsaken Islaam, such as the areas of the Juhayna clan and other tribes belonging to the Qudaa'ah tribe. When he reached Waadi Qura, Hadhrat Usaama (RA) sent a spy ahead from the Banu Udhra tribe, whose name was Hurayth. Taking to his mount, he rode ahead of Hadhrat Usaama (RA) until he reached Ubna (their intended destination). He surveyed the area and searched for the best route (for the army to take). He then returned quickly and rejoined Hadhrat Usaama (RA) at a place that lay a distance of two nights journey from Ubna. He informed Hadhrat Usaama (RA) that the people were oblivious of the (Muslim) army and had not even mustered their own army. Hadhrat Usaama (RA) then ordered the Muslim army to move speedily and attack the enemy unawares before they had a chance to muster their forces. [^1]
Hadhrat Usaama (RA) Seeks Permission to Return to Madinah but Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Refuses Permission

Hadhrat Hasan bin Abil Hasan narrates that before he passed away, Rasulullaah ﷺ formed an army comprising of the people of Madinah and surrounding areas. Included in this army was Hadhrat Umar (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid (RA) as the Ameer of this army. The last man of the army had not yet passed by the trench when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away.
